summary: Round 19 recheck, 27 Sep 17:32-18:25Z. At the 18:04:40Z poll header probes 45 and 46 were still PENDING. Picks: three closed ideas that no round from 2 to 18 re-checked (51 items were skipped). All three trace back to one closure rule: the round-13 division-PP rule 'a knob needs a lab sign >= 0 on BOTH embryos', from research/wf_ideas_v4/round13/scan_hyp_division_pp.json R13DP-1..5. That rule's own top pick was dc0.30: positive on both embryos, bootstrap P(<0) = 0.00, 0 TP lost. It then read -0.005 on the public board (probe 41). So the rule does not predict the public sign. All three were re-measured on CPU on the exp70b-like bed (x138 lab replay + #35 insertion + forkmid 4.5). Beds: exp60 (56 clips) and exp64 (71 44b6 clips). tools/ was not changed. (A) REVISED: I-051/I-334, symmetry tau 0.6 -> 0.75. It was closed as 'embryo-specific, not a rung'. On the exp70b bed: 6bba +0.0043 (+6 TP / +5 FP, TPs spread over 6 clips), 44b6 exp60 0.0000, 44b6 exp64 -0.0013 (0 TP / +4 FP). New facts point to the public embryo behaving at least like 6bba for fork ADDs that stay at DeepCenter >= 0.25. The tau gate runs AFTER the DC >= 0.25 gate, and 44-49% of the forks tau adds sit in DC [0.25, 0.30). Probe 41 showed that band is TP-rich on the public board, while the lab says 0 TP there. The insertion added forks and gained +0.001 on the public board on 3 of 3 stacks, while 44b6 lab ~0. Public division J (0.22-0.36) is above both lab embryos. forkmid removes only 7 of 167 tau-added forks, so the two stack. New verdict: the strongest untested existing-knob division lever. It is admissible as ONE public-only rung, exp70b + tau 0.75, under the user's 11:14/11:16Z aggressive-mode lift; no tau ladder. Estimates: P(display >= 0.955) ~0.35-0.5, P(<= 0.953) ~0.2-0.3. Private EV is uncertain (a 44b6-like embryo gives -0.001). It becomes a final only by the user's re-tick. (B) UPHELD, stronger: I-333, divergence 2.25 -> 2.5. On the exp70b bed: 6bba +0.0009 (removes 4 FP, 0 TP), 44b6 0. This is the same 'removes only lab-FP forks' signature as dc0.30, which flipped to -0.005 on the public board, and 37-55% of the removed forks are in the DC [0.25, 0.30) band. The GT-geometry reason (implied band precision ~0.37 > 0.265) now has public support. Do not build it. (C) CORRECTED: I-053 (open division gates, RESULTS.md l.50) stays closed on lab grounds. However, the 12:12Z CONTEXT line (R17-A3) quoted amanatar V6 (0.901) as public proof that 'more divisions via looser gates can crash', and that citation is wrong. The -0.052 is larger than the whole division term (<= 0.036 by probe 26) plus added-fork edges. V6 does not touch tau, and it bundles a new max-consensus detection blend, DET 0.960 and retention 0.75. V6 is not a read on division gates and cannot be held against (A). No submit, push, commit or Kaggle post was made. Finals stay #37 + #38.

findings.what: I-051 / I-334: loosen the safe-division symmetry gate from SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU 0.6 to 0.75. It is an existing x138 knob, needs zero new code and adds no runtime. OLD VERDICT: RESULTS.md l.73 (11 Sep, old base, 14 GT divisions) found 'tau 0.6 (public) best'. Round 13 R13DP-4 then re-measured it on x138: 6bba +0.005, 44b6-71 -0.0009..-0.0017. It was 'embryo-specific: do not ladder it, do not put it in a final', and the density-aware version I-334 went to the post-deadline list. The closure rested on two premises: (1) the both-embryo lab-sign rule; (2) 'the public embryo type is a coin flip'. WHAT CHANGED: (a) Premise 1 is falsified for the public direction. dc0.30 was the rule's flagship pick: positive on both embryos, bootstrap P(<0) 0.00, 0 TP lost. It read -0.005 on the public board (probe 41). (b) Premise 2 is no longer a coin flip for ADDs above DC 0.25. In x138 cell 5 (l.1544-1609) the gates are conjunctive and tau is checked AFTER the DeepCenter >= 0.25 gate, so every tau-added fork is a DC >= 0.25 fork. Of those, 44-49% sit in DC [0.25, 0.30). Probe 41 showed that band is TP-rich on the public embryo (removing 20 dummy forks there cost -0.005), while the lab calls it pure FP (6bba 0 TP / 6 FP / 116 ignored). The insertion (an ADD) gained +0.001 on the public board on 3 of 3 stacks, while the 44b6 lab is ~0. Public division J (0.22-0.36) is above both lab embryos. Justin CH123's division-only 0.953 -> 0.956 on x138 (I-311) is the kind of public jump a tau change would produce. (c) Re-measured today on the exp70b-like bed (K2 lab replay + #35 insertion + forkmid 4.5): 6bba +0.00434 (div TP/FP 23/22 -> 29/27; added forks 6 TP / 5 FP / 92 ignored; the 6 TPs are in 6 different clips out of 10 clips with an evaluable change); 44b6 exp60-17 -0.000003 (57 added, 0 evaluable); 44b6 exp64-71 -0.00126 (0 TP / 4 FP / 291 ignored). forkmid 4.5 removes only 7 of 167 and 6 of 301 tau-added forks, so tau and exp70b's forkmid do not interfere. (d) The user lifted the FREEZE and the public-rung ban at 11:14/11:16Z (aggressive mode), and 28 Sep has 5 slots. NEW VERDICT: REVISED from 'closed for the LB' to 'admissible as ONE public-only rung on exp70b'. It is the best-evidenced existing-knob division lever not yet probed. It stays class C/public-aimed and needs no pre-R8 lab gate, because it is a knob under the user's lift, not a new mechanism. Honest odds (model estimate, prior-dependent): P(display >= 0.955) ~0.35-0.5; P(<= 0.953) ~0.2-0.3; public swing up to about +0.004 if 6bba-like, -0.001 if 44b6-like. The private (71%) sign depends on embryo type, with EV slightly positive under a 60/40 mix, so it is never a final without the user's re-tick. I-334 (a density-aware gate) stays post-deadline because it is new code.

findings.what: I-053, 'open gates (drop symmetry/divergence) + floor + sister-first ranker' (RESULTS.md l.50; FP explodes, 27-29 FP), plus the public evidence recently attached to that family. The 12:12Z CONTEXT entry (R17-A3) reads amanatar V6 at 0.901 (-0.052 vs x138) as 'a public read that more divisions via looser gates can crash'. RE-CHECK: V6 does not change tau. It changes 8 knobs: DET 0.965 -> 0.960, gap 5.8, SAFE_DIV_MAX 10.5, SISTER 15, divergence ~off through a new 3-frame lookahead, caps 0.012/0.006, short-track rescue, and retention 0.90 -> 0.75. It also adds new detection code: a z-scored secondary with a max-consensus blend. Arithmetic: the division term is at most 0.1*J_pub <= 0.036, per probe 26 (all forks off = -0.036, an upper estimate). Even J -> 0 plus every added fork edge counted as FP (~+650 edges on ~117k) stays below 0.052. So at least ~0.011 of V6's loss, and likely most of it, comes from the detection and node changes. NEW VERDICT: I-053 itself stays closed on its lab evidence (divergence 1.75 lab -0.0017; open gates flood FP). The V6 citation is a misattribution and must not be used against division ADD rungs such as R19-RC-A. V6 is confounded and says nothing about division gates.
